cites.quote: No background jobs exist yet. Reminders or clean-ups would be the first.
`appointment_event` records every change with time and actor.
Hospital time zone Asia/Kolkata, currency INR.
A `Periodic background job` in the API finds overdue Scheduled appointments and sets them to Stale

findings.suggested_fix: Add an unknown and a non-blocking question for the job interval (or the maximum delay before marking), with a proposed default.
findings.text: REQ-6 says a periodic job marks Stale but gives no run interval or latency bound. Without one, nobody can check how soon after the 24-hour window an appointment must show as Stale.

cites.quote: wherever an appointment's status is shown (lists, appointment page) (`Also add a list filter`)

findings.suggested_fix: Drop the filter quote from REQ-9 and keep it only in REQ-11.
findings.text: REQ-9 (show the label) quotes the A-06 answer 'Also add a list filter', which belongs to REQ-11. The label requirement reads as if it were about the filter.

cites.quote: Back-filling: the job's first run marks every existing overdue Scheduled appointment

findings.suggested_fix: Either make it an assumed REQ with a basis, or phrase it only as 'no separate data migration: not asked in the ticket'.
findings.text: The out-of-scope back-filling item asserts a behaviour (the first run marks every existing overdue appointment) with no cite and no REQ. That is a decision recorded as an exclusion.

questions.text: How often should the Stale background job run, or what is the longest allowed delay between the 24-hour window ending and the appointment showing as Stale?

rubric_items.reason: All four ticket acceptance criteria map to REQ-1 to REQ-4; the window, mechanism, actor and UI follow-ups are covered, and the out-of-scope items give reasons.
Most REQs are atomic and checkable. REQ-6 gives no run interval, so a tester cannot check how soon an overdue appointment becomes Stale.
Every known REQ cites the ticket, the pack or an IDE answer. The out-of-scope back-filling line states job behaviour with no cite.
The glossary clashes (only Scheduled changes, actor always staff) were asked as Q-03/Q-04, answered, and recorded as mismatches with cites.
Q-05 is non-blocking, has real options and is correctly scoped. The job interval was never asked.
Readable and uses glossary terms. REQ-9 quotes the list-filter answer, which confuses the label requirement with REQ-11.
